title: Sections of a two-open etale cover form an equalizer
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], U,V opens with U ∨ V = top, and F an abelian sheaf on X.smallEtaleTopology [def-weil-pbc-etale-site, def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves]. Put a(s)=(s|U,s|V), and b(s,t)=s|U∩V-t|U∩V, using the open-immersion restrictions. Then a is injective and Function.Exact a b. No injectivity assumption on F is needed.

source.place: Tag 0A50, proof: first and middle spots, via the sheaf condition

proof.text: The inclusions U → X and V → X form a covering of the small etale site: their underlying scheme maps have ranges U and V, and the cover hypothesis says their union is all X. This is checked with Scheme.ofArrows_mem_smallEtaleTopology_iff and Scheme.Opens.range_ι.

The scheme pullback of the two open inclusions is U∩V, with its two inclusion maps (isPullback_opens_inf, the open-fibre-product fact). On a cone of compatible sections, apply the sheaf amalgamation axiom to the Bool-indexed covering. For a relation with equal indices cancel the monomorphic open immersion. For a relation with different indices lift the pair of maps through the intersection pullback, then use the cone relation and functoriality of restrictions to verify compatibility.

The amalgamation axiom gives the cone map with its two required composites; separatedness gives uniqueness. Thus the section square is a pullback in abelian groups. Forgetting to sets preserves this limit. The equivalence between a limiting cone point and {(s,t) | s|=t|} proves the section injection and supplies a preimage for every pair killed by the difference. Conversely, restrictions of a global section agree by the square relation.

    (hcover : U ⊔ V = ⊤) (F : Sheaf X.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) :
    Function.Injective (fun x : F.obj.obj (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X))) =>
      (F.obj.map (MorphismProperty.Over.homMk
        (A := Scheme.Etale.mk U.ι) (B := Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X))

       F.obj.map (MorphismProperty.Over.homMk
        (A := Scheme.Etale.mk V.ι) (B := Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X))
        V.ι (Category.comp_id V.ι)).op x)) ∧
    Function.Exact (fun x : F.obj.obj (op (Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X))) =>
      (F.obj.map (MorphismProperty.Over.homMk
        (A := Scheme.Etale.mk U.ι) (B := Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X))
        U.ι (Category.comp_id U.ι)).op x,
       F.obj.map (MorphismProperty.Over.homMk
        (A := Scheme.Etale.mk V.ι) (B := Scheme.Etale.mk (𝟙 X))
        V.ι (Category.comp_id V.ι)).op x))
      (fun x => F.obj.map (MorphismProperty.Over.homMk
        (A := Scheme.Etale.mk (U ⊓ V).ι) (B := Scheme.Etale.mk U.ι)
        (X.homOfLE inf_le_left) (X.homOfLE_ι inf_le_left)).op x.1 -
        F.obj.map (MorphismProperty.Over.homMk
        (A := Scheme.Etale.mk (U ⊓ V).ι) (B := Scheme.Etale.mk V.ι)
        (X.homOfLE inf_le_right) (X.homOfLE_ι inf_le_right)).op x.2)

blueprint_update.statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $U,V\subseteq X$ open subschemes with $U\cup V=X$, and $F$ an abelian sheaf on the small étale site $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let $a:F(X)\to F(U)\oplus F(V)$, $a(s)=(s|_U,s|_V)$, and $b:F(U)\oplus F(V)\to F(U\cap V)$, $b(s,t)=s|_{U\cap V}-t|_{U\cap V}$, all restrictions being along the open immersions. Then $a$ is injective and $\ker b=\operatorname{im}a$, i.e. $0\to F(X)\xrightarrow{a}F(U)\oplus F(V)\xrightarrow{b}F(U\cap V)$ is exact. No injectivity assumption on $F$ is needed.

proof.text: The inclusions $U\to X$ and $V\to X$ are open immersions, hence etale, and their images $U$ and $V$ cover $X$; so they form a covering of $X$ in the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. The fibre product of the two open immersions is $U\cap V$ with its two inclusions, and $U\times_XU=U$, $V\times_XV=V$ because open immersions are monomorphisms.

The sheaf condition for this covering says that $F(X)\to F(U)\times F(V)\rightrightarrows F(U\times_XU)\times F(U\times_XV)\times F(V\times_XU)\times F(V\times_XV)$ is an equalizer. The components indexed by equal indices impose no condition, since $U\times_XU=U$ and the two restrictions to it agree; the components indexed by different indices compare the restrictions to $U\cap V$. Hence $s\mapsto(s|_U,s|_V)$ identifies $F(X)$ with the set of pairs $(s,t)\in F(U)\times F(V)$ with $s|_{U\cap V}=t|_{U\cap V}$.

This says exactly that $a$ is injective and that every pair with $b(s,t)=0$ is $a(r)$ for some $r\in F(X)$. Conversely $b\circ a=0$, since the restrictions of a global section to $U\cap V$ through $U$ and through $V$ agree by functoriality of restriction. So $0\to F(X)\xrightarrow{a}F(U)\oplus F(V)\xrightarrow{b}F(U\cap V)$ is exact.
